claims.title: Magan supplies copper to Mesopotamia
claims.summary: Sumerian texts record a land called Magan, identified with Oman, as a source of copper and diorite carried by sea to the city-states of Mesopotamia.

claims.title: Beehive tombs and towers at Bat
claims.summary: The Bronze Age communities of Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn raised monumental stone towers and dry-stone beehive tombs, later inscribed by UNESCO in 1988 as the most complete such collection in the world.

claims.title: The frankincense trade flourishes in Dhofar
claims.summary: The resin of the Boswellia sacra tree, harvested in Dhofar, became one of antiquity's great luxury goods, carried by caravan and ship from southern Arabia to the Mediterranean.

claims.title: Khor Rori and the incense ports

claims.title: Madha's elders choose Muscat; Nahwa stays with Sharjah
claims.summary: According to local oral history, the leaders of the neighbouring ruling families asked the elders of the mountain village of Madha which ruler it wished to follow. Madha chose Oman, reportedly for its perceived wealth, stronger government and the protection of its water, while the nearby village of Nahwa stayed with the Qawasim of Sharjah. The choice left Madha an Omani exclave inside the Trucial Coast with a Sharjah village inside it. The date and the wording of the question are recorded only in oral accounts.

sources.label: Madha village's pledge of allegiance changed the map forever
A hidden piece of the Emirates

claims.title: The Madha and Nahwa boundary is fixed
claims.summary: After British surveyors consulted local tribes and rulers, the boundary between Madha and Nahwa was settled in 1969, two years before the federation, making Madha an exclave of Oman and Nahwa a counter-enclave of Sharjah. The line was inherited by the United Arab Emirates in 1971.
